title: Platform systems & services — team playbook, dashboards, runbooks and roadmap (2026)
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document is the central team playbook for the Platform Systems & Services area. It combines: an inventory of critical services, ownership and RACI, the canonical dashboards and alerting thresholds, runbook procedures for common incidents, how-to checklists for onboarding services, a short retrospective summary, and the near-term roadmap. The goal is to provide a single reference engineers can use during on-call, planning, and operational handovers.

Scope

- Services owned by Platform Systems & Services (platform-api, routing-service, autoscaler, kv-cache-service, batch-worker, observability-ingest).
- Dashboards and alerting owned by the observability subteam (OBS).
- On-call and runbooks for tier-0/tier-1 incidents; higher-level product incidents are cross-team.

Key contacts and ownership

- Primary owner: Platform Systems & Services (team alias: team-platform-systems).
- On-call rotation: platform-oncall (pagerduty).
- Program lead: Maya Chen (author).
- Observability lead: Ravi Patel.

RACI (high level)

- Deployments: Platform Infra (R) / Platform Services (A) / Eng-SRE (C) / Product (I)
- Alerts tuning: Observability (R) / Platform Services (A) / Eng-SRE (C)
- Runbook ownership: Platform Services (R/A)

Systems & services inventory (summary)

| Service | Primary owner | SLOs | Critical dashboards | Data plane | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| platform-api | team-platform-systems | availability 99.95%; p99 latency < 300ms | API Latency / Errors | REST + gRPC | Front-door for internal platform requests |
| routing-service | team-platform-systems | availability 99.9%; p95 latency < 200ms | Routing P95/P99 / Error rate | gRPC | Routes to model endpoints and autoscaler |
| kv-cache-service | team-platform-systems | cache hit rate >= 80% | Cache hit/miss, memory | Redis-compatible | Prefix caching for inference KV |
| autoscaler | team-platform-systems | scale-to-target latency < 45s | Scale events, queued requests | Kubernetes + custom controller | Handles burst policies and reserved pools |
| observability-ingest | team-observability | ingest availability 99.9% | Ingest lag, retention | Kafka -> ClickHouse | Critical for dashboards and alerts |
| batch-worker | team-platform-systems | job success rate >= 99% | Job queue depth, failures | Kubernetes CronJobs | Background tasks: cleanup, backfills |

Canonical dashboards and alerts

Overview: Observability provides a set of standardized dashboards and templated alerts. Below are the high-priority dashboards and the alerting thresholds used for on-call paging. All alert rules live in the repo infra/observability/alerts and are reviewed during SLO triage.

Priority dashboards

1) Platform Overview (team-platform-systems) — uptime, p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, QPS by route, deployment version rollout heatmap.
2) Routing Service Dashboard — p95/p99 latency, backend error codes, active route map, KV cache hit rate.
3) Autoscaler Dashboard — desired vs actual replicas, scale events per minute, blocked scaling queue, API throttle rate.
4) Observability Ingest — Kafka consumer lag, ingest throughput, storage retention pressure.

Alerting thresholds (paging)

| Alert name | Condition (example) | Severity | Runbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| platform-api-high-latency | p99 latency > 350ms for 3m | P1 | platform-api-p1-runbook |
| platform-api-error-rate | 5xx rate > 1% for 5m | P1 | platform-api-p1-runbook |
| routing-service-backend-errors | backend 5xx > 0.5% for 5m | P1 | routing-service-p1-runbook |
| autoscaler-failed-scaling | any scale failure OR failed to reach desired replicas for 2x scaling windows | P1 | autoscaler-p1-runbook |
| observability-ingest-lag | kafka consumer lag > 100k for 10m | P1 | observability-ingest-p1-runbook |
| kv-cache-low-hit-rate | cache hit rate < 60% for 10m | P2 | kv-cache-p2-runbook |

Alerting playbook (what to do when a P1 page fires)

1. Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty within 2 minutes. Check the primary dashboard for the named service.
2. Triage to determine scope: is it regional or global? Is traffic intact? Are downstream dependencies failing?
3. If the issue is service degradation (latency or errors):
   - Clear recent deployments: surface last deploys from CI and rollback if the deploy correlates with onset.
   - Check autoscaler and queue metrics; if queue is growing, scale capacity or enable burst.
4. If ingestion/backing systems are failing: open an incident and notify Eng-SRE and Observability leads; switch to degraded mode if available.
5. For any P1 longer than 30 minutes, create an incident channel, assign an incident commander, set 15-minute update cadence.

On-call runbook: quick actions (cheat-sheet)

1) Identify service status: use the Platform Overview dashboard and service-specific dashboard.
2) Command center commands (shortcuts):
   - kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=platform-api
   - kubectl -n platform rollout undo deployment/platform-api --to-revision=PREVIOUS_REV
   - infra/scripts/scale-to.sh autoscaler 50  # scale autoscaler to 50 replicas (example)
3) Check recent deploys in CI: CI link is pinned in the dashboard header.
4) Check logs: central logging (Loki) query examples:
   - {app="platform-api"} |= "ERROR" | json
5) If an emergency rollback is performed, add a postmortem tag to the deployment and open a postmortem doc template.

How-to: onboard a new service to Platform systems

Follow these steps to onboard a service so it benefits from standard dashboards, alerts and SLOs.

1. Pre-onboarding checklist (owner: service owner)
   - Service repo exists in our GitHub org and follows repo template.
   - Has a Kubernetes manifest and Helm chart.
   - Health endpoints: /health/live and /health/ready.
   - Metrics exported via OpenMetrics (Prometheus format) with the standard metric prefix 'platform_'.
   - CI includes integration tests and a smoke test.
2. Create an onboarding PR to infra/observability/monitoring with:
   - a dashboard JSON (Grafana v9) using the platform dashboard template.
   - alert rules (yaml) using the standard alert template.
   - recommended SLOs and SLI definitions (p99/p95 latency and availability).
3. Observability reviews PR (2 business days SLA). After approval: deploy dashboard and alerts to staging and run golden traffic tests.
4. Finalize SLO and add to SLO registry (infra/slo-registry).

Example alert rule (Prometheus + Alertmanager)

---
groups:
- name: platform-api.rules
  rules:
  - alert: PlatformAPIHighLatency
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="platform-api"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.35
    for: 3m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "Platform API p99 latency high (>350ms)"
      description: "p99 latency for platform-api exceeded 350ms for 3 minutes. See Platform Overview dashboard"

How-to: add a new dashboard tile

1. Use the dashboard template (grafana/dashboards/platform-template.json).
2. Create a draft dashboard in the staging Grafana namespace.
3. Validate metric names and variables against the metric catalog.
4. Open PR to infra/observability/dashboards. Include screenshots and query samples.
5. Observability review and merge. Schedule a 24-hour monitoring window to ensure no noisy alerts.

Runbooks (links and summary)

- platform-api-p1-runbook: immediate checklist for API P1s, rollback play, and mitigation steps.
- routing-service-p1-runbook: backend mapping, circuit-breaker reset, and route isolation steps.
- autoscaler-p1-runbook: manual scale steps, cache warmup guidance, and rollout of burst capacity.
- observability-ingest-p1-runbook: consumer restart sequence and retention emergency procedures.

Retrospective (Q4 2025 summary and action items)

Summary:
- We experienced three P1 incidents related to autoscaler and one major ingest lag event. Root causes were a regression in scale decision logic and a misconfigured Kafka consumer group during a rolling upgrade.

What went well:
- Improved incident comms: channels and update cadence were followed.
- Post-incident hotfixes reduced recurrence window.

What to improve and action items:
1. Autoscaler: add integration test that simulates burst traffic and verifies scale-to-target latency (owner: autoscaler team; target: 2026-04-15).
2. Observability: introduce consumer-group upgrade checklist and safe-defaults for rolling upgrades (owner: observability; target: 2026-03-31).
3. Runbooks: add rollback automation to reduce human error during emergency rollbacks (owner: platform infra; target: 2026-05-01).

Roadmap (near-term priorities)

Q2 2026:
- Autoscaler v2: improved decision logic, safer burst handling, and canary rollout. (owner: platform-services)
- SLO first drive: publish team-level SLOs and connect to alerting playbooks. (owner: observability)
- Dashboard consolidation: remove redundant panels and standardize variables. (owner: observability)

Q3 2026:
- Platform private deployment improvements: hardened network defaults and onboarding checklist for customer-private clusters. (owner: eng-private-deployments)
- Cost-optimized batching experimentation with new quantization-aware batcher. (owner: serving-runtime)

Maintenance cadence and ownership

- Dashboard and alert reviews: quarterly (observability lead).
- Runbook review: every 6 months or after any P1 incident (runbook owner).
- Onboarding reviews: rolling SLA of 2 business days for observability reviews.
